newsitem.title: HAITI: Former Haitian president denies role in violence.
newsitem.headline: Former Haitian president denies role in violence.

text.p: Former Haitian President Jean-Bertrand Aristide has denied any responsibility for recent violent anti-government demonstrations that led up to the resignation this week of Prime Minister Rosny Smarth.

In an interview published on Thursday in the Creole-language newspaper Liberte, Aristide said he did not sanction violence, especially as a way to better the lives of Haiti's people. "There is no one that can stand with violence in his speech and in his actions and think that he can save this country," he said.

Aristide said adherents of his opposition political party, Fanmi Lavalas, have also been targets of violence. "How do we react? With consciousness, we ask for togetherness, we ask for non-violence, we ask for respect. Everyone is free to choose the political party they want," he said.

Paul Dejean, a longtime political ally of Aristide's, who was Cabinet minister for Haitians living abroad until Smarth's resignation, recently told journalists Aristide had "an immense ambition for power," and that he was responsible for the tension, insecurity and disorder in the capital.

Haiti has for the past few months been rocked by general strikes and violent demonstrations by popular organisations that opposed the government's economic plans and called for Smarth's resignation. Aristide, who last November split with the ruling Lavalas Political Organisation to form his own party, also publicly criticised the government programme.

In his resignation speech, Smarth said he had had enough of the current political situation. "About the political plan, I don't agree with the way the game is being played, without principle, without ethics," he said.
